name: Brake System & Hydraulic Safety
disclaimer: Brakes are your primary safety system. Any loss of braking efficiency is an immediate life safety hazard.

symptoms: Brake pedal feels soft, spongy, or sinks all the way to the floorboard
potentialCauses: Brake hydraulic line leak / blown brake hose
Severely contaminated brake fluid with air bubbles
subtopics.criticalWarning: SAFETY HAZARD: DO NOT DRIVE THE VEHICLE. If moving, use emergency/parking brake gradually and downshift to lower gears to stop. Arrange immediate flatbed tow.
triageQuestions: Does pumping the brake pedal build pressure or does it keep sinking?
Do you notice clear or amber oily fluid on inside of tyres or under car?
subtopics.recommendedAction: Immediate Towing & Complete hydraulic brake line / master cylinder inspection.

symptoms: Metal-on-metal harsh grinding noise when stopping
potentialCauses: Brake pad wear indicator scraping rotor
Pads completely worn down to backing plate (grinding)
subtopics.criticalWarning: Metal-on-metal grinding means bare backing plate is chewing into rotor, increasing stopping distance dramatically and causing rotor damage.
triageQuestions: Is it a squeak or a heavy metallic grinding?
Does the vehicle pull to one side when you brake?
subtopics.recommendedAction: Brake pad & rotor replacement and calliper slide lubrication.

symptoms: Steering wheel shakes vigorously when slowing down from highway speeds
triageQuestions: Does the shaking happen only while pressing the brake pedal, or all the time at highway speeds?
subtopics.recommendedAction: Rotor runout measurement, rotor resurfacing or replacement, and pad bedding.

triageRules: Treat soft/failing pedal as IMMEDIATE ESCALATION / NON-DRIVABLE.
Advise customer that friction materials have legal minimum thickness limits (usually 3mm).
